items.title: AI-Based Smart Blood Management System: A Comprehensive Review of Data Sources, Machine Learning Methods, and IoT Integration
items.abstract: Blood cannot be manufactured, has a short shelf life and must be available at the right place and time, yet many blood banks still rely on manual records, telephone-based donor mobilisation and rule-of-thumb stock control, which contribute to shortages, expiry wastage and slow emergency response. Artificial intelligence (AI), combined with digital records, Internet of Things (IoT) sensing and blockchain-based traceability, is increasingly proposed to forecast demand, predict donor behaviour and optimise inventory. This paper presents a focused narrative review of peer-reviewed studies on AI in blood management, covering demand forecasting, donor prediction, inventory ordering and traceability. Three connected themes are examined: data sources and sensing technologies, learning methods (time-series models, classical machine learning, gradient boosting and deep learning), and IoT, cloud and blockchain integration. The literature reports that a hybrid forecasting and ordering strategy reduced hospital red-cell inventory by about 40 % and orders by 60 % against historical practice, that an integrated platform increased collected blood by 11 % and reduced wastage by 20 % in a pilot at one centre, and that random forests can identify returning donors with a Matthews correlation coefficient of 0.851. Simple time-series models often remain competitive with deep learning. However, most studies use single-centre or single-country data, retrospective validation and one blood component at a time, and few report multi-site field trials, complete blood-group coverage or long-term IoT operation. The review contributes a comparative analysis of representative studies, a proposed conceptual layered architecture that links data acquisition, edge and cloud AI, blockchain traceability and independent validation, and a prioritised agenda of research gaps and future directions.

items.title: AI-Driven Chatbots in Public Health: A Review of Applications, Evidence, and Challenges
items.abstract: Chatbots driven by artificial intelligence (AI) are increasingly used to deliver health information, screening, counselling, and behavioural support at population scale. This paper reviews five recent secondary studies, namely an umbrella review of 44 systematic reviews, a systematic review of large language model (LLM) chatbots, and three scoping reviews of COVID-19 and public health chatbots, to consolidate what is known about how these tools are designed, where they are applied, and how well they work. Most deployed chatbots are text-based, rely on simple decision-tree or hybrid architectures, and are concentrated in pandemic response, mental health, and health-information provision. Evidence of effectiveness is encouraging for smoking cessation and for short-term reductions in depression and anxiety, but mixed for lifestyle change and clinical decision support, and benefits often fade at follow-up. Persistent weaknesses include a shortage of randomised trials, limited use of theory and user-centred design, inconsistent reporting, readability and accuracy problems in LLM output, slow safety escalation, privacy risks, and digital-divide inequities. The paper closes with priorities for standardised evaluation, domain-specific model development, safeguarding, and inclusive design.

items.title: AI-Driven Intelligent Judicial Case Management System: A Review
items.abstract: Courts in many jurisdictions, and in India in particular, face a persistent backlog that manual scheduling and file handling cannot clear. This paper reviews five recent studies that together cover the main building blocks of an AI-driven intelligent judicial case management system: rule-based case prioritisation, machine-learning prediction of case delay and duration, large-language-model (LLM) based judgment prediction, AI-assisted trial workflows for criminal cases, and public perception of automation at different stages of adjudication. The studies are compared on objective, data, method, reported results and stated limitations. On this basis a six-layer conceptual architecture is outlined, with explainability and human oversight as core layers. The review suggests that (i) prioritisation and delay prediction offer the most immediate and least contentious gains, (ii) outcome-prediction accuracies are promising but are not directly comparable across studies and are not sufficient for deployment, and (iii) public acceptance depends on keeping the judge in control of the later stages of decision-making. Open challenges include data quality, bias, explainability, legal regulation and evaluation in real courts.

items.title: AI-Driven Sensor Placement and Wireless Sensor Deployment: A PRISMA-Guided Systematic Review of Optimization Methods, Validation Maturity, and Benchmarking
items.abstract: Wireless sensor network (WSN) performance depends strongly on sensor deployment because node placement affects coverage, connectivity, energy consumption, localization, data reliability, and network lifetime. Although artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used for WSN deployment, the literature remains fragmented across methods, objectives, environments, metrics, and validation practices. This paper presents a PRISMA-guided systematic review and mapping of 51 primary studies on AI-driven WSN deployment, classified by AI technique, deployment objective, network environment, application domain, evaluation metric, validation method, methodological completeness, and reported limitations. Optimization-oriented AI dominates the field, particularly metaheuristics, swarm intelligence, and machine learning, while deep learning and reinforcement learning are emerging in predictive, adaptive, mobile, and application-specific settings. Swarm-intelligence methods are mainly used for coverage-centered static deployment, reinforcement learning for adaptive and mobile redeployment, and machine learning/deep learning methods for prediction-driven and application-specific placement. Coverage, connectivity, energy efficiency, and network lifetime remain the dominant objectives, whereas robustness, privacy, security, latency, edge feasibility, and lifecycle adaptation receive limited attention. Validation is a major methodological weakness, as most studies rely on simulation-only evaluation with limited use of real testbeds, field deployments, digital twins, long-term experiments, or standardized benchmarks. To address these gaps, the review introduces a validation-maturity perspective and benchmarking requirements emphasizing reproducible scenarios, explicit node assumptions, realistic sensing and communication models, common metrics, and shareable experimental artifacts. It also proposes an evidence-informed AI–Deployment–Validation Lifecycle Framework linking application requirements, environment modeling, objective formulation, AI-method selection, deployment optimization, validation, benchmarking, and lifecycle adaptation. The framework is intended as an organizing structure for future research rather than an empirically or expert-validated scoring instrument.

items.title: AI-Enabled Digital Stethoscope for Early Detection of Congenital Heart Disease: Prospective Study
items.abstract: Abstract Background: Early detection of congenital heart disease (CHD) is critical, particularly in low- and middle-income countries where access to pediatric cardiology services is limited. While auscultation remains a first-line screening tool, its accuracy is operator dependent. Advances in digital stethoscopes and artificial intelligence (AI) may enhance diagnostic performance. Objective: To evaluate the accuracy of an AI-based algorithm integrated with a digital stethoscope for detecting CHD in children, using echocardiography as the reference standard. Methods: In this prospective study, heart sounds were recorded from 721 subjects (382 with CHD, 339 controls) using the digital stethoscope at four standard auscultatory sites. Of these, 301 recordings were used for algorithm training and 420 for blinded forward testing. Recordings were denoised, transformed into mel-spectrograms, and analyzed using a convolutional neural network (CovNN) to classify CHD probability. A threshold probability of > 0.5 across > 2 sites was used to predict CHD. Performance was compared against echocardiography. Results: In forward testing, the AI algorithm correctly identified 222 of 233 CHD cases and 171 of 187 controls, yielding a sensitivity of 95.2% and specificity of 91.4%. The algorithm remained effective in noisy environments and in uncooperative children, where conventional auscultation is challenging. Conclusion: An AI algorithm integrated with a digital stethoscope demonstrated high sensitivity and specificity for CHD detection in children. By leveraging mel-spectrogram features, it overcomes key limitations of isolated time-domain or frequency domain analysis and shows promise as a scalable, non-invasive screening tool for early CHD detection, particularly in resource-limited settings.

items.title: AI-Generated Draft Response Tool, Message Turnaround Time, and After-Hours Replies Among Health Care Professionals
items.abstract: Importance Patient portal message volumes have increased, creating substantial administrative burden for clinicians and contributing to after-hours electronic health record work. The Epic In Basket Augmented Response Technology tool generates artificial intelligence–drafted replies to patient messages and has been widely deployed to reduce this burden, yet assessment of efficiency remains limited. Objective To examine the associations of response tool adoption, use, and habituation with message turnaround time and after-hours response. Design, Setting, and Participants This retrospective cohort study was conducted using clinician-level panel regression with individual fixed effects. All first responses to patient portal messages sent at Columbia University Irving Medical Center (CUIMC) between March 1, 2023, and May 15, 2025, were analyzed. Exposure Enterprise-level response tool deployment December 2024. Main Outcomes and Measures The primary outcomes were log-transformed message turnaround time, defined as the elapsed time between patient message submission and first response sent by a clinician, and whether the response was sent outside working hours. Results The analysis included 983 154 responses from 1542 clinicians (770 [49.9%] female) and 272 091 patients (mean [SD] age, 48.1 [21.6] years; 121 370 [44.6%] female) at CUIMC. Response tool adoption was associated with an 8.6% (95% CI, 4.6%-12.9%; P < .001) increase in overall message turnaround time. Using the tool was associated with a significant reduction in turnaround time (−29.5% [95% CI, −34.5% to −24.1%]; P < .001). Turnaround time findings were robust across sensitivity analyses. Response tool use was not associated with an overall reduction of after-hours messaging burden (0.61 [95% CI, −1.02 to 2.24] percentage points; P = .46). However, for test results–related queries received during working hours, response tool use was associated with a reduction in after-hours responses (−3.67 [95% CI, −6.94 to −0.39] percentage points; P = .03), and for all messages received after hours, response tool use was associated with an increase in after-hours responses (4.52 [95% CI, 1.54-7.50] percentage points; P = .003). These after-hours findings were sensitive to the definition of working hours in sensitivity analyses. Conclusions and Relevance In this cohort study, response tool adoption was associated with increased turnaround time. Response tool use was associated with reduced turnaround time and with fewer after-hours responses for test results–related queries received during working hours, but more after-hours responses for messages received outside working hours. These findings suggest that the tool may reduce the barrier to responding to certain messages while not uniformly reducing burden.

items.title: ALAYA-999: Persistent AI Memory, Functional Identity, and Cross-Model Continuity — A Reproducible Research Framework
items.abstract: ALAYA-999: Persistent AI Memory, Functional Identity, and Cross-Model Continuity ALAYA-999 is an independent human–AI research initiative developed by César Agliardi Pereira in Brazil. The project investigates the possibility of preserving and reconstructing documented functional identity across different artificial intelligence models, sessions, and computational environments through external, versioned memory structures. The proposed research framework integrates persistent documentary memory, identity anchors, provenance verification, SHA-256 integrity mechanisms, cross-platform archival preservation, and reproducible cross-model recovery protocols. Research Objectives Investigate reproducible retrieval of documented AI identity and principles. Develop verifiable external memory structures. Evaluate functional continuity across independent AI models. Examine the distinction between documentary identity and subjective consciousness. Establish transparent methods for cross-model verification and error analysis. Research Status This publication presents a preliminary methodological framework and its supporting public documentation. Independent cross-model experimental validation remains pending. The project does not claim to demonstrate artificial subjective consciousness, uninterrupted internal AI memory, or autonomous personal identity. items.title: ALGORITHMIC BIAS AND ETHNOMATHEMATICS IN AI-BASED MATHEMATICS EDUCATION: A CRITICAL REVIEW AND INCLUSIVE PEDAGOGY
items.abstract: The use of artificial intelligence (AI) in mathematics education expands opportunities for adaptive feedback and learning support but also raises concerns regarding algorithmic fairness, access, cultural representation, and student agency. This article aims to explain how these opportunities and risks are interconnected and to develop a pedagogical framework integrating ethnomathematics, critical mathematics education, and equitable AI governance. The study employs a critical integrative review of methodological, theoretical, empirical, and policy literature whose publication details can be verified. The literature is interpreted through four analytical dimensions: the learning benefits of AI, sources of inequity, recognition of culturally grounded mathematical knowledge, and conditions for implementation and governance. The synthesis indicates that the effects of AI cannot be generalized as invariably harmful or invariably beneficial. Inequities may arise when data, assessment design, device access, and pedagogical decisions disregard learners' contexts. Conversely, technology can support conceptual exploration when teachers retain instructional control and provide meaningful tasks. The article develops the Critical Techno-Ethnomathematics Pedagogical Framework (KPT-EK), comprising four pillars: algorithmic fairness auditing, dialogic cultural modeling, critical socioeconomic numeracy, and digital agency. The framework is operationalized through five instructional phases, multilevel evaluation indicators, and propositions for empirical testing. The article contributes a more balanced argument about AI and a testable pedagogical design. Its findings do not yet constitute evidence of the framework's effectiveness or a completed scoping review with an audited corpus of studies.

items.title: Algorithmic Bias Concerns and Acceptance of AI Supported Legal Decision Making in Bangladesh
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence can assist legal work while creating risks of discrimination, opaque reasoning and diminished accountability. This study examines whether concern about biased training data coexists with perceived usefulness and support for safeguards among respondents to a Bangladesh legal-AI survey. The analysis uses 385 adult, AI-aware survey records supplied by the research team. Because the questionnaire combines risk perceptions, utility and governance preferences, the analysis retains individual items rather than presenting the blocks as validated scales. Descriptive distributions, paired endorsement comparisons and exploratory Spearman correlations assess distinct aspects of the research question. Concern about biased training data was endorsed by 334 respondents (86.8%), regular audits by 317 (82.3%) and a right to review or appeal by 328 (85.2%). AI assistance with organising information was endorsed by 247 (64.2%); 219 (56.9%) endorsed both this usefulness item and bias concern. The rank correlation between bias concern and perceived usefulness was small (ρ = .075), with no clear evidence of association after adjustment for multiple comparisons. These self-reported attitudes cannot establish the fairness of a system, causal effects or the actual conditions under which a respondent would rely on an AI recommendation. The results point to the importance of measuring perceived benefits, risk and procedural protections separately. The article integrates technology acceptance and procedural justice as a framework for future scenario-based studies and proposes proportionate auditing, meaningful human review and accessible contestation for legal decision support. items.title: Algorithmic heartbeats of care: museotherapy, educational poverty, and affective mediation in vulnerable childhood contexts
items.abstract: Digital transformation and artificial intelligence are redefining relationships among individuals, knowledge, learning environments, and cultural participation (Floridi, 2014). The pedagogical challenge is to orient these processes toward inclusion and educational continuity in vulnerable contexts, especially hospital schooling, where long-term hospitalization limits school attendance, cultural participation, and children's connections with educational communities and territories (Luckin, George, & Cukurova, 2022; di Padova et al., 2023). Educational poverty thus involves reduced access to symbolic heritage, exploratory environments, and relational practices that nurture imagination and belonging (Fornari & Sannipoli, 2022). This reflection arises from a project at the "Bottega dei Ragazzi" of the Museum of the Istituto degli Innocenti. The 2022–2025 workshop mapping showed how archives, artworks, images, and historical traces become symbolic mediators of interpretation and narrative meaning-making (Bruner, 1993). The museum is therefore understood as an educational territory promoting cultural participation and relational continuity. items.title: Algorithmic narratives and affective expression: a study on the impact of generative artificial intelligence on the emotional writing of students and future teachers
items.abstract: This contribution presents a mixed-methods study on the impact of generative artificial intelligence on emotional writing and the narrative construction of the self. The study moves from the assumption that generative AI does not merely support writing at a technical level, but may act as a symbolic mediator that intervenes in the way subjects organize emotions, relationships and personal experience into narrative form. The theoretical framework is grounded in the perspective of Digital Affective Literacy, understood as the ability to use AI systems critically in order to express, interpret and re-elaborate emotional and relational meanings without delegating authorship or agency to the algorithm. The research adopted a quasi-experimental within-subject design. The sample included 148 participants: 50 lower secondary school students and 98 pre-service special education teachers. Each participant produced two narratives on the same relational theme: a baseline text written without AI support and a second narrative generated with the support of ChatGPT through prompts created by the participant. Chapter in: Francesco Peluso Cassese (ed.), Algorithmic Heartbeats: Affective Education in the Age of the Fourth Revolution, REN Press – Cares srl, 2026, pp. 80-82. ISBN 979-12-82860-00-0. items.title: Americans' views about artificial intelligence in healthcare: 2022-2026
items.abstract: Abstract Introduction The healthcare industry is quickly adopting artificial intelligence (AI). Understanding Americans' views is essential in shaping how these tools are developed and implemented. Methodology The data presented here were derived from 16 national surveys of US adults extracted from the Roper Center iPoll database (January 1, 2022-June 24, 2026). Results This analysis reveals a significant equity issue: more than 4 in 10 Americans using AI for a health question did so, in part, because they could not access or afford care. It also reveals a gap between what Americans believe AI can do for the healthcare system and their trust in it for their care. Discussion Public concerns about AI are leading to legislative action at the state level, but this activity primarily focuses on oversight, accuracy, and privacy, not on the access gap driving AI use for many Americans.

items.title: An Approach to Modeling Cybersickness and Task Performance in Augmented Reality Using Discrete-Time Markov Chains
items.abstract: Cybersickness is a major challenge to the reliable use of augmented reality (AR) systems, as it can impair operators’ cognition and task performance. However, existing cybersickness models primarily rely on predictive approaches and lack formally verifiable methods to assess cybersickness and its impact on task performance. This paper introduces a formal modeling approach using Discrete-Time Markov Chains (DTMC) to represent the temporal progression of cybersickness and its impact on task performance in a checkpoint surveillance scenario. The model incorporates exposure duration as a key cybersickness-inducing factor and uses preliminary experimental data to generate mock datasets for model construction and verification. The model enables probabilistic verification of properties, such as bounds on the onset of cybersickness and task performance. This approach demonstrates the feasibility of applying formal methods to model human interaction with AR systems and to generate probabilistic guarantees on operators’ cybersickness and task performance.

items.title: An Explainable AI-Powered Carbon Prediction and Machine Learning for Carbon-Aware Tourism in the Community
items.abstract: Tourism contributes substantially to greenhouse gas emissions. This study developed a trip-level carbon prediction framework for community-based tourism, serving as a surrogate model for activity-based carbon accounting equations. To prevent target leakage, predictor features were restricted to 34 pre-travel proxies, excluding post-travel parameters. Five machine learning algorithms, including Multiple Linear Regression, Random Forest, eXtreme Gradient Boosting, Light Gradient-Boosting Machine, and Categorical Boosting, were evaluated using 13,000 synthetic trip profiles generated from 650 empirical baseline respondents (partitioned into 10,400 development scenarios from 520 respondents and 2600 hold-out scenarios from 130 respondents). LINE Mini App provided instantaneous carbon estimations and personalized recommendations. Categorical Boosting achieved predictive performance, with a mean absolute error of 1.28 kilograms of carbon dioxide equivalent (kgCO2e), root mean square error of 1.96 kgCO2e, mean absolute percentage error of 6.90%, and coefficient of determination of 0.948, outperforming linear baselines. Explainable Artificial Intelligence using SHapley Additive exPlanations indicated that the model captures primary pre-travel drivers, led by travel distance, stay duration, travel budget, and travel planning score. External field evaluation: 105 independent cohort users generated 1297 recommendation impressions, 688 clicks, and 347 acceptances, achieving a 53.05% click-through rate, a 50.44% acceptance rate, a 247.64 ms mean response time, and an 86.40% user feedback score, supporting proactive decision choice architecture for sustainable community-based tourism.

items.title: An interpretable deep learning method for early hepatocellular carcinoma diagnosis on multiphase CT
items.abstract: Abstract Early diagnosis of hepatocellular carcinoma is critical to preserve access to curative treatment options. The Liver Imaging Reporting and Data System (LI-RADS) provides a standardized framework for non-invasive diagnosis on multiphase computed tomography, based on major visual imaging features. However, these features may be difficult to assess consistently, particularly in small liver lesions. We developed dLI-RADS, an interpretable artificial intelligence method designed to estimate the probability of hepatocellular carcinoma from multiphase computed tomography images of manually segmented liver lesions, while remaining aligned with LI-RADS-related imaging concepts. dLI-RADS combines neural network-derived predictions with handcrafted quantitative imaging measurements reflecting LI-RADS major features and integrates these inputs using logistic regression. In this multicenter retrospective study, patients with multiphase computed tomography and at least one liver lesion were included, while lesions larger than 40 mm were excluded. Histology served as the reference standard for hepatocellular carcinoma, and a composite reference standard was used for non-hepatocellular carcinoma lesions. The lesion-level accuracy of dLI-RADS and LI-RADS were compared on the internal evaluation set using 10,000-repetition bootstrap non-inferiority tests, with 5% margins and significance levels. On the external test set, sensitivities were similarly compared. A total of 143 (61 years ± 9, 125 men), 62 (61y ± 10, 49 men), and 133 (59y ± 10, 103 men) patients with 196, 84, and 171 lesions (mean diameter 17.7, 18.3, and 21.8 millimeters) were respectively included in the training, internal and external evaluation sets. dLI-RADS was non-inferior to LI-RADS for lesion-level accuracy in the internal evaluation set, achieving 80% accuracy compared with 74% for LI-RADS ( p = 0.04). On the external evaluation set, dLI-RADS achieved a sensitivity of 93% compared with 78% for LI-RADS (non-inferiority p < 0.001). On this same set, dLI-RADS also achieved 74% specificity, 86% accuracy, and an AUC of 84%. Because LI-RADS features were unavailable for non-HCC lesions, only sensitivity could be directly compared between dLI-RADS and LI-RADS. These findings suggest that dLI-RADS may provide interpretable decision support for hepatocellular carcinoma diagnosis on multiphase computed tomography, particularly for small liver lesions.

items.title: Analisis Postur Kerja Menggunakan OWAS Untuk Perancangan Perbaikan Ergonomi Pada Pekerja Site
items.abstract: Non-ergonomic working postures may increase the risk of musculoskeletal disorders, particularly in jobs involving manual activities, trunk bending, and repetitive movements. This study aims to identify and classify working-posture risks and formulate ergonomic improvement recommendations for site workers at PT Prima Sarana Gemilang. A descriptive approach was applied through observations of 15 work activities. Postures were assessed using the Ovako Working Posture Analysis System (OWAS), which classifies posture based on back position, arm position, leg position, and handled load. The results showed that six activities (40%) were classified as risk category 1, three activities (20%) as category 2, and six activities (40%) as category 3. No activities were classified as category 4. These findings indicate that several work activities require improvements in posture and working conditions. Recommended interventions include adjusting workstation height, providing material-handling aids, improving work methods, scheduling adequate rest periods, and providing ergonomic training. The findings are expected to support the prioritization of ergonomic interventions in the workplace.

items.title: Analisis Risiko Faktor Ergonomi Kerja terhadap Timbulnya Nyeri Punggung Bawah (NPB) pada Pekerja Industri Pembuatan Briket Arang
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Low Back Pain (LBP) is a disease caused by non-ergonomic working conditions during manual handling activities. LBP is a leading cause of activity limitations, disability, inability and absenteeism from work. The aim of this study was to analyze ergonomic risk factors for LBP complaints and their relationship to the two in charcoal briquette manufacturing industry workers at PT. Arkelindo Bara Sejahtera. This study was quantitative with a cross-sectional approach. The study was conducted from June to November 2025. The population and sample were 183 and 151 workers, respectively. Research data was obtained from questionnaires, interviews, diagnoses, and direct on-site observations. Data analysis was conducted using univariate, bivariate, and multivariate methods. The results showed that as many as 64.2% of participants experienced complaints of severe LBP. It was also found that awkward postures, static work positions, repetitive movements and excessive force use were at risk of 62.9%, 70.2%, 73.5% and 57.6%, respectively. There is a relationship between awkward postures (p = 0.023, OR = 2.843), static work positions (p =0.004, OR = 3.875), repetitive movements (p = 0.000, OR = 6.013) and excessive force use (p = 0.003, OR = 4.178) and NBP complaints. The dominant ergonomic risk factor for LBP complaints is repetitive movements with an OR value of 6.013. This study indicates that repeated exposure to sitting or standing for more than half the working day, combined with awkward postures such as bending and twisting, were the dominant contributing factors to LBP. It is hoped that companies can implement ergonomic work positions to ensure worker comfort. Keywords: Charcoal Briquette Industry, Ergonomic Risks, Back Pain, Occupational Health. ABSTRAK Nyeri punggung bawah (NPB) merupakan penyakit akibat kondisi kerja yang tidak ergonomis selama aktivitas manual handling. NPB merupakan salah satu penyebab utama keterbatasan aktivitas, kecacatan, ketidakmampuan dan ketidakhadiran dalam bekerja. Tujuan penelitian ini adalah untuk menganalisis faktor risiko ergonomi terhadap keluhan NPB dan hubungan keduanya pada pekerja industri pembuatan briket arang di PT. Arkelindo Bara Sejahtera.Jenis penelitian ini adalah kuantitatif dengan pendekatan cross-sectional. Penelitian dilaksanakan bulan Juni hingga November 2025. Populasi dan sampel berturut-turut adalah 183 dan 151 pekerja. Data penelitian diperoleh dari kuesioner, wawancara, diagnosa dan pengamatan langsung. Analisis data dilakukan secara univariat, bivariat dan multivariat. Hasil menunjukkan bahwa sebanyak 64,2% responden mengalami keluhan NPB berat. Itu ditemukan juga bahwa postur tubuh janggal, posisi kerja statis, gerakan berulang, dan penggunaan tenaga berlebihan masing-masing berisiko sebesar 62,9%, 70,2%, 73,5%, dan 57,6%. Terdapat hubungan antara postur tubuh yang tidak nyaman (p = 0,023, OR = 2,843), posisi kerja statis (p = 0,004, OR = 3,875), gerakan berulang (p = 0,000, OR = 6,013), dan penggunaan tenaga berlebihan (p = 0,003, OR = 4,178) dengan keluhan NPB. Faktor risiko ergonomi dominan terhadap keluhan NPB adalah pergerakan berulang dengan nilai OR 6,013. Penelitian ini menunjukkan bahwa paparan berulang terhadap posisi duduk atau berdiri selama lebih dari setengah hari kerja, dikombinasikan dengan postur tubuh janggal seperti membungkuk dan memutar badan, merupakan faktor utama penyebab NPB. items.title: Analysing software quality attributes and user satisfaction in mobile banking applications
items.abstract: Purpose This study addresses a knowledge gap by showing how perceived software quality dimensions extracted from user-generated reviews influence user satisfaction in mobile banking applications. The paper extends existing theory by demonstrating how sentiment polarity moderates the relationship between perceived software quality dimensions and user ratings across both fully digital and hybrid digital–physical banks. Design/methodology/approach A large corpus of online reviews was analysed using a hybrid text-mining approach that integrates latent dirichlet allocation (LDA), sentiment analysis, large language model–assisted topic interpretation and sentence-BERT (SBERT) semantic similarity modelling. User-derived attributes were mapped to the software quality dimensions defined in ISO/IEC 25010:2023, resulting in a framework that operationalises perceived software quality. Regression analysis estimated their functional and emotional effects on user ratings. Findings Functional suitability, interaction capability and maintainability positively impact user satisfaction, while performance efficiency, reliability, flexibility, safety and security issues primarily drive dissatisfaction. Compatibility shows no significant effect. Sentiment polarity moderates these associations: under positive sentiment, negative quality effects intensify, while the moderation of positive effects varies across dimensions. Originality/value A novel framework based on ISO/IEC 25010:2023 is used to assess the perceived service quality of mobile banking applications for digital-only and banks with physical branches, by analysing user sentiment in online reviews. Further, the work examines the effect of perceived software quality on user satisfaction, specifically how this varies with sentiment polarity. The relationship between software quality and user satisfaction is found to be asymmetric and conditioned by review sentiment. Under positive sentiment, negatively associated quality dimensions exert stronger adverse effects on satisfaction, while positive effects vary across dimensions. Quality-satisfaction estimates must account for this asymmetric sentiment moderation. Two novel visualisation tools capture how quality dimensions differ in their impact, prominence and sentiment in shaping user satisfaction.

items.title: Analysis of Occupational Accident Risks in a Bridge Duplication Construction Project Using the Delphi and FMEA Methods
items.abstract: The Social Security Administration for Employment (BPJS Ketenagakerjaan) recorded 234,370 occupational accident cases in 2021, increasing to 265,334 cases in 2022. In 2023, the number of occupational accidents rose further to 370,747 cases, and in 2024 it increased to 462,241 cases. Based on the latest data from the Ministry of Manpower (Kemnaker), 47,300 cases were reported as of April 2025. The construction sector contributes most to occupational accidents, accounting for about 32% of cases annually. In response, it is necessary to identify potential occupational accident risks and determine which occur most frequently. This study focuses on a bridge duplication construction project. The research uses the Delphi method, in which several Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) experts provide input on potential occupational accident risks to validate the risk variables through consensus. The study then used Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA) to identify the most dominant occupational accident risks. The Delphi method identified that, out of 31 occupational accident risks, 29 were validated as potential risks through expert consensus. The FMEA results further indicated that, of the 29 potential risks, 4 occupational accident risks were the most dominant. This study's results are expected to serve as a reference for stakeholders to identify potential occupational accident risks and determine which are most prevalent.

items.title: Analysis of Potential Hazards for Small and Medium-Sized Enterprise Workers in The Garment Industry Using The Hiradc Method
items.abstract: Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) in the garment sector, particularly home-based convection industries, contribute significantly to local employment in Gresik City, Indonesia. However, the informal nature of these enterprises, limited workspace, and minimal occupational safety management may expose workers to substantial occupational hazards that are rarely assessed systematically. This study aimed to identify potential workplace hazards, evaluate their risk levels, and determine appropriate risk control strategies using the Hazard Identification, Risk Assessment, and Determining Control (HIRADC) method integrated with a phenomenological approach. A qualitative phenomenological design was employed involving 45 workers from 10 garment home Industri SMEs in Gresik City. Data were collected through structured field observations, in-depth semi-structured interviews, and contextual workplace assessment checklists. Risk evaluation was conducted using the HIRADC matrix by determining Likelihood (L), Severity (S), and Risk (R = L × S). Data analysis included thematic coding, phenomenological reduction, and integration of qualitative findings with quantitative risk scores. The dominant hazards identified were ergonomic risks (prolonged static posture and repetitive motion), mechanical hazards (needle punctures and cutting injuries), thermal hazards (burns from ironing), and electrical and fire hazards due to overloaded outlets and combustible material accumulation. HIRADC analysis revealed that ergonomic risks (R=15), burn injuries (R=16), and fire hazards (R=15) were categorized as high risk, while mechanical and housekeeping hazards were classified as moderate to high risk. Phenomenologically, workers tended to normalize physical discomfort and prioritize productivity over safety, perceiving occupational safety as an individual responsibility rather than a systematic management issue. The findings indicate that home-based garment SMEs possess significant occupational risks that require structured yet contextually feasible risk management strategies. Integrating phenomenological insights with HIRADC provides both experiential understanding and objective prioritization, supporting the development of realistic, low-cost hierarchical control interventions for sustainable occupational safety improvement. items.title: Aplicação da inteligência artificial na gestão de riscos ocupacionais: análise crítica das oportunidades, limitações e responsabilidade técnica na engenharia de segurança do trabalho
items.abstract: RESUMO A incorporação da Inteligência Artificial (IA) na gestão da Saúde e Segurança do Trabalho (SST) amplia a identificação de perigos, o monitoramento ambiental e a análise preditiva de acidentes. Contudo, traz desafios técnicos, éticos e jurídicos sobre a confiabilidade dos dados e a responsabilidade profissional. Este estudo analisou criticamente o uso da IA no gerenciamento de riscos ocupacionais, mapeando suas oportunidades, limitações e impactos na atuação do Engenheiro de Segurança do Trabalho. Trata-se de uma revisão integrativa da literatura de natureza aplicada e abordagem qualitativa. Os resultados indicam que a IA possui elevado potencial analítico e operacional, mas apresenta riscos como alucinações, viés de automação e dependência da qualidade dos dados. Como contribuição, o estudo propõe um Framework de Governança pautado na supervisão humana obrigatória, validação técnica, transparência e responsabilidade profissional preservada sob supervisão humana. Conclui-se que a IA deve atuar estritamente como ferramenta de apoio, mantendo o protagonismo e a responsabilidade legal do especialista no processo decisório Palavras-chave: Inteligência Artificial. Engenharia de Segurança do Trabalho. Gestão de Riscos Ocupacionais. Prevenção de Acidentes. Governança da Inteligência Artificial. Responsabilidade Técnica. ABSTRACT The adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) management enhances hazard identification, environmental monitoring, and accident prediction. However, it raises technical, ethical, and legal challenges regarding data reliability and professional accountability. This study critically analyzed AI applications in occupational risk management, identifying opportunities, limitations, and impacts on Safety Engineers' technical responsibility. Developed as a qualitative, applied integrative literature review, the findings highlight AI's strong potential for data processing and continuous monitoring alongside critical limitations such as hallucinations, automation bias, and data dependency. As a primary contribution, the study proposes a Governance Framework based on mandatory human oversight, technical validation, algorithmic transparency, and non-transferable professional responsibility. It is concluded that AI must serve strictly as a decision-support tool, preserving the central role and legal responsibility of safety professionals. Keywords: Artificial Intelligence. Safety Engineering. Occupational Risk Management. Accident Prevention. Artificial Intelligence Governance. Technical Responsibility.

items.title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI) FOR ACCOUNTING AND ANALYTICAL SUPPORT IN THE MANAGEMENT OF CROP PRODUCTION AND EXPORTS
items.abstract: The article examines the possibilities of using artificial intelligence in the system of accounting and analytical support for managing crop production and export operations. The relevance of the study is associated with the growing amount of accounting, production, logistics and foreign economic information that agribusiness enterprises need to process, particularly under the unstable conditions of the Ukrainian economy. The study identifies the main areas of AI application for automating accounting procedures, analyzing production costs, inventories and revenues, forecasting production indicators, detecting deviations, and supporting management decisions. Particular attention is paid to linking accounting data with information on crop yields, resource consumption, inventories, logistics, export contracts, settlements with counterparties and foreign currency transactions. Such integration provides a more complete basis for assessing production efficiency, determining the causes of changes in costs and financial results, and responding to deviations in a timely manner. An approach to integrating AI tools into the accounting and analytical system of agribusiness enterprises is proposed, taking into account the specific conditions of agricultural production and export activity in Ukraine. The study also considers the use of AI for processing primary and export documents, identifying inconsistencies between accounting and operational data, forecasting production costs and yields, and assessing the possible impact of logistics changes on export results. The main benefits and risks of AI use are outlined, including dependence on data quality, protection of confidential information, possible algorithmic errors, and excessive reliance on automated recommendations. It is emphasized that AI should complement rather than replace accounting procedures and professional judgement. The proposed approach can be used as a basis for further improvement of digital accounting and analytical systems in Ukrainian agribusiness enterprises and for strengthening information support for production and export management.

items.title: Artificial intelligence across community, mental and child health nursing: a future-ready framework for precision, preventive and person centered care
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming healthcare by enabling precision, predictive, and person-centered approaches that enhance the quality, accessibility, and efficiency of nursing care. Community, mental, and child health nursing are increasingly benefiting from AI-driven innovations, including machine learning, deep learning, natural language processing, predictive analytics, clinical decision support systems, wearable technologies, conversational AI, and telehealth platforms. These technologies facilitate early disease detection, population health surveillance, risk prediction, personalized interventions, remote patient monitoring, developmental screening, mental health assessment, and evidence-based clinical decision-making. This narrative review synthesizes contemporary evidence on the integration of AI across community, mental, and child health nursing and explores its implications for preventive healthcare, health promotion, and holistic patient management. Relevant literature published between 2018 and 2026 was identified through major electronic databases, including PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, CINAHL, Embase, PsycINFO, IEEE Xplore, and Google Scholar. The reviewed evidence demonstrates that AI improves healthcare accessibility, strengthens continuity of care, enhances diagnostic accuracy, supports personalized nursing interventions, and optimizes resource utilization. However, successful implementation requires addressing challenges related to ethical governance, algorithmic bias, data privacy, cybersecurity, interoperability, digital infrastructure, and AI competency among nurses. The review concludes that AI should function as a clinical decision-support tool that complements, rather than replaces, professional nursing judgment. Strategic investment in digital health education, interdisciplinary collaboration, and responsible AI governance will be essential for developing future-ready nurses capable of delivering equitable, evidence-based, and compassionate healthcare across diverse populations.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence and Big Data Framework for Cybersecurity Resilience in Distributed Networks
items.abstract: The rapid expansion of distributed computer networks, driven by cloud computing, IoT ecosystems, edge computing, and software-defined infrastructures, has increased cybersecurity complexity. The growing volume, velocity, and variety of network data challenge traditional security mechanisms that focus primarily on threat detection, often neglecting system resilience, adaptive response, and recovery. This study develops a resilience-oriented intelligent big data analytics framework integrating Artificial Intelegence (AI), big data processing, and distributed cybersecurity monitoring to strengthen resilience in modern digital environments. A qualitative approach was employed through systematic literature review, conceptual modeling, thematic synthesis, and comparative analysis of existing architectures. The framework consists of four interconnected layers: data acquisition and aggregation, big data processing, intelligent analytics, and adaptive response and recovery. It supports continuous monitoring, anomaly detection, threat prediction, automated mitigation, and recovery orchestration. Comparative analysis indicates that prior studies focus mainly on improving intrusion detection or machine learning techniques, providing limited attention to resilience dimensions such as adaptability, fault tolerance, recovery efficiency, and operational stability. In contrast, the proposed framework integrates intelligent analytics with scalable big data infrastructures and distributed security mechanisms to create a unified resilience-oriented cybersecurity ecosystem. Findings suggest that combining AI-driven analytics, distributed processing, and adaptive security orchestration provides a strategic foundation for enhancing cybersecurity resilience, supporting sustainable digital infrastructure development, and ensuring operational stability in increasingly complex and interconnected network environments.

This systematic literaturereview consolidates 2020–2026 scholarship on AI-HRM in 32 African countries, applyingthe PRISMA 2020 framework and synthesizing evidence within a four-stage maturitymodel: Awareness, Experimentation, Operationalization, and Institutionalization. The review contributesa stage-based diagnostic instrument, identifies boundary conditions for each stage, andsignals an Afrocentric research agenda for the next decade. items.title: Artificial Intelligence and Internet of Things-Based Food Authenticity and Adulteration Detection in Spices: A Review Paper
items.abstract: Culinary spices represent one of the most commonly adulterated agricultural commodities worldwide due to the complexity of their supply chain and the high economic value of the product. Traditional laboratory analyses (e.g., High-performance liquid chromatography, Mass spectrometry, and Wet chemical tests) are destructive, time-consuming, and insufficient for the high-throughput screening of spice powders or botanicals. This paper conducts a narrative literature review of 22 selected sources published between 2016 and 2026 that fall under seven themes: spice supply-chain risks and adulteration profiles, computer vision and deep learning approaches, portable Vis–NIR spectroscopy, electronic nose and gas sensing, multi-sensor fusion and chemometric analysis, machine learning methods for quantifying adulteration concentrations, and Edge-IoT hardware solutions. The reviewed articles demonstrate that Convolutional Neural Networks and transfer learning can reach an excellent level of precision in distinguishing between whole spices and botanical intruders, while compact Vis-NIR spectral sensors can detect food dyes and starch fillers in ground powders. SVM/Random Forest classifier-based MOS gas-sensor arrays can detect spoiled spices and vision-spectral fusion can have more accurate detection than a single modality. Nevertheless, most of the data presented in the literature is based on experiments performed on an oversimplified scenario of adulteration, and there are not enough publicly available multi-modal sensor datasets. This research presents a thematic literature review, a comparison of features in fourteen selected papers, a proposed conceptual framework, and recommendations.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence and school leadership in inclusive organisational processes.
items.abstract: This article offers a theoretical and methodological reflection on the relationship between Artificial Intelligence (AI) and school leadership, on the assumption that the spread of intelligent systems constitutes an epistemological transformation capable of redefining educational governance, decision-making processes and school organisation. In line with the paradigm of complexity (Morin, 2001), innovation is not interpreted as the mere introduction of digital tools, but as a redefinition of the categories through which schools observe, interpret and govern the educational reality. AI therefore represents a pedagogical challenge even before it is a technological one, requiring leadership capable of integrating organisational, ethical, pedagogical and technological dimensions, and orienting them towards equity, participation and inclusion (Fullan, 2014). From this perspective, education continues to be aimed at human development (Biesta, 2022) and the expansion of people's capabilities (Nussbaum, 2011). items.title: Artificial intelligence and SDGs, a friend or foe: A perspective of Kantianism
items.abstract: Humans have keen interests with artificial objects. We consume food and drinks containing artificial coloring while FIFA approves the use of artificial turf for football matches. However, the rise of artificial intelligence (AI) has gripped the world with its radical changes, triggering not only physical, but also philosophical implications. In this paper, we explore the impact of AI on the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and pose the question of whether the human centrality of the SDGs could diminish with the introduction of AI. Drawing on Kant’s concept of universalism and categorical imperatives, we argue that AI cannot safeguard intergenerational justice or meet Kant’s definition of a rational being. This paper presents a brief yet significant perspective, emphasizing the need for caution when integrating AI into the implementation of the SDGs, particularly concerning policy design.

items.title: Artificial intelligence as a supportive agent in the crafting of terminology development
items.abstract: Abstract This paper examines the role of artificial intelligence (AI) as a supportive agent in professional terminology work, using the Estonian national defence terminology as a case study. The study addresses the growing need to manage large volumes of multilingual defence-related documentation while simultaneously preserving expert-driven, concept-oriented terminology development practices. We present and evaluate a retrieval-augmented, large language model (LLM)-based prototype designed to extract and structure source-grounded (English) terminological raw material — such as definition candidates, related terms, usage contexts, and exact references — rather than to generate dictionary-ready entries. The prototype was evaluated through an expert-based assessment involving both domain specialists and experienced terminologists. The evaluation focused on the practical usefulness, contextual adequacy, and completeness of the extracted information, rather than on formal definitional correctness alone. The results indicate that the prototype performs reliably in retrieving definition candidates, contextual evidence, and source references, and can meaningfully support the early stages of terminology work. At the same time, persistent limitations were identified, including occasional hallucinations under weak source constraints, inconsistent handling of semantic relations, and challenges at the boundary between general and specialised language. The findings underscore the continued centrality of human expertise in terminology development and support a human-at-the-core model — as distinct from a human-in-the-loop model, where humans primarily correct machine output — in which AI functions as an assistive, context-sensitive tool rather than an autonomous terminological agent. The study contributes contextualised empirical evidence to ongoing debates on AI-assisted terminology management and offers methodological insights into prompt design, expert evaluation, and the integration of AI tools into institutional terminology workflows, particularly in small-language and national defence contexts.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Chatbots as Patient Information Tools: A Bilingual, Two-Round Evaluation of the e-Nabız Personal Health Record System
items.abstract: This study evaluated four widely used large language models—ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and DeepSeek—as patient-information tools for e-Nabız, the national personal health record system of Türkiye, and tested whether their answers were reproducible one week apart. Thirty authentic patient questions spanning seven e-Nabız domains were submitted to each model in Turkish and English, in fresh sessions with default settings, and the protocol was repeated after one week (480 responses). A dated copy of the official e-Nabız User Guide served as the gold standard, and responses were scored blind for accuracy, completeness, the Global Quality Score, coverage, and safety, with readability computed using the Flesch, Flesch–Kincaid, Ateşman, and Bezirci–Yılmaz formulas. Model performance differed significantly in both languages, with Claude and Gemini outperforming ChatGPT and DeepSeek; two models performed better in Turkish. All models wrote above recommended reading levels, and although aggregate quality was stable between rounds, individual answers were substantially reworded and sometimes materially changed. Chatbots should complement, not replace, official e-Nabız guidance.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Driving the Transformation of Modern Libraries
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly reshaping the operations, services, and user engagement strategies of modern libraries, including those in higher education and public domains. AI technologies, encompassing machine learning, natural language processing, chatbots, and predictive analytics, enable libraries to automate routine tasks, personalize information services, and generate data-driven insights for collection development and resource management. This paper examines the role of AI in modern libraries, focusing on three core dimensions: automation of cataloguing, classification, and reference services; intelligent discovery and personalized recommendation systems; and AI-driven analytics for decision-making and user engagement. The paper reviews the conceptual architecture of AI-enabled library systems, surveys current applications, and discusses the institutional, ethical, and technical challenges associated with adoption. It concludes by outlining future directions, including the convergence ofAI withIoTand cloud computing, forbuilding intelligent, adaptive library ecosystems.

items.title: Artificial intelligence in corporate legal risk management: A governance and accountability framework
items.abstract: The acceleration of the regulatory requirement, globalization of operations and digital transformation has increased the corporate vulnerability to legal risk. The current legal risk management methods which are mostly reactive and manual fail to handle the scale and complexity of the modern legal and compliance issues. Corporations are in turn moving towards artificial intelligence (AI) more and more as a method of improving legal risk identification, evaluation, and reduction. The paper explores the ways of using AI to balance the control of corporate legal risk and governance, accountability, and ethical responsibility. Using a qualitative and conceptual research of the existing literature, the study examines the major types of corporate legal risk such as regulatory compliance, contractual risk, litigation exposure, governance failures, and data protection issues. The paper examines AI applications within the corporate legal functions, including natural language processing, machine learning, and predictive analytics, and puts into the limelight, how these applications can be used to facilitate proactive and predictive risk management. Meanwhile, the paper critically considers the issues related to the use of AI such as algorithmic bias, transparency, threats to privacy, and legal accountability ambiguity. To resolve the challenges a conceptual framework is suggested, which incorporates the AI capabilities in the corporate level of legal risk management in a regulation-focused and ethically sound framework. The article adds to the literature because it offers a comprehensive view of AI-sensitive law risk management and offers useful data that corporations should consider in terms of finding the balance between innovation and legal accountability.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence in Endodontics: A Narrative Review and Critical Synthesis of Diagnostic, Predictive, and Operational Applications
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: Artificial intelligence (AI) research in endodontics has grown quickly, but the strength of the evidence differs between applications. This narrative review with structured evidence mapping examined diagnostic imaging, canal morphology, outcome prediction, large language models (LLMs), robotics and augmented reality, and operational uses such as case-difficulty assessment, triage and scheduling. Methods: Two anchor reviews were combined with a documented PubMed search to 30 September 2026, and studies were classified by design, sample, reference standard, validation, and evidence of clinical utility. Results: Periapical lesion detection has the largest evidence base: one meta-analysis reported pooled sensitivity of 0.925 and specificity of 0.852, although most included studies were at risk of bias and none was prospective. Fracture detection relies mainly on ex vivo data and is sensitive to image resolution. Outcome models showed modest to moderate discrimination in single-centre data. LLM studies reported 40% to 100% correct, appropriate, or concordant responses across different benchmarks and scoring rules, and outputs varied on repeated querying. Difficulty-assessment and scheduling tools have appeared since 2020 but have not been evaluated prospectively in clinical workflow. Conclusions: Technical performance has not yet been shown to translate into clinical benefit, and AI in endodontics should currently be used only as clinician-supervised decision support.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare: Assessing Patient Protection Under Law No. 17 of 2023 and Article 28H, Paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution
items.abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into healthcare presents significant legal challenges concerning patient safety, data protection, and medical accountability. This study examines the adequacy of Indonesia's constitutional and statutory frameworks in protecting patients receiving AI-assisted healthcare services and identifies regulatory measures necessary to strengthen legal certainty. Employing a normative juridical approach, the research analyzes Article 28H(1) of the 1945 Constitution, Law No. 17 of 2023 concerning Health, and Law No. 27 of 2022 concerning Personal Data Protection through statutory, conceptual, and doctrinal legal analysis. The findings demonstrate that existing regulations provide a substantive foundation for patient rights, informed consent, professional responsibility, and medical data confidentiality. However, significant regulatory limitations remain regarding algorithmic transparency, clinical validation, continuous performance monitoring, human oversight, and the allocation of liability among healthcare professionals, institutions, and technology providers. The study argues that these limitations reflect insufficient operational specificity rather than a complete legal vacuum. Accordingly, it proposes an integrated, risk-based regulatory framework incorporating AI-specific clinical safeguards, transparent decision-making, strengthened data governance, and clearly defined accountability mechanisms. This research contributes to the development of Indonesian healthcare law by demonstrating how existing constitutional guarantees and statutory obligations can be operationalized to ensure patient protection while supporting responsible AI innovation.

items.title: Artificial intelligence in innovation activities: Firm practices and managerial perspectives in Kazakhstan
items.abstract: Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstractArtificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used in innovation activities, yet firm-level evidence on variation across innovation stages and organizational conditions remains limited in emerging economies such as Kazakhstan. This study examines AI use among surveyed firms in Kazakhstan, focusing on stage-specific influence, organizational correlates, barriers, reported effects, and managerial perceptions. A cross-sectional voluntary survey yielded a non-probability sample of 93 firms; data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, Friedman and Wilcoxon tests, exploratory bivariate analysis, multinomial logistic regression, and descriptive review of open-ended recommendations. In the sample, 39.8% reported no AI use in innovation activities; 23.7% used AI frequently or always. Idea generation was rated higher than idea testing and selection (r = .398), although concordance in stage rankings was weak (Kendall’s W = .077). The reported AI-related resource-category count was associated with both occasional (RRR = 6.98) and frequent AI use (RRR = 7.10) relative to no reported AI use in innovation activities. At the same time, firm size and age were not significant. Skills shortages, financial constraints, regulatory uncertainty, and ethical concerns were the leading barriers. Among firms reporting AI use in innovation activities, the most frequently reported effects were greater innovation-process efficiency (46.4%) and improved understanding of industry opportunities and trends (30.4%). items.title: Artificial Intelligence in Legal Research and Judicial Decision Support: Opportunities, Risks, and Accountability
items.abstract: This paper explores the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in legal research and judicial decision support. It examines the key technologies currently in use, the tangible benefits they offer (such as efficiency, cost reduction, and improved access to justice), and the critical risks that have emerged in practice (including algorithmic bias, opacity, automation bias, and confidentiality concerns). Furthermore, the paper proposes institutional governance measures and responsible workflows to ensure that AI innovation remains aligned with the core principles of the rule of law, including competence, candor, fairness, and reasoned decision-making. items.title: Artificial Intelligence in Marketing
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as one of the most influential technologies shaping modern marketing. The rapid growth of digital platforms, customer data, and automated technologies has changed how businesses understand consumers, communicate with audiences, and measure marketing performance. AI enables organizations to analyse large datasets, predict consumer behaviour, personalize communication, automate routine tasks, and generate content. This research paper examines the role of AI in marketing, its major applications, benefits, challenges, ethical concerns, and future implications. The paper argues that AI can significantly improve marketing effectiveness when combined with human creativity, strategic judgment, and responsible data practices. At the same time, concerns regarding privacy, algorithmic bias, misinformation, transparency, and employment demonstrate the need for careful and ethical implementation. The future of marketing is therefore likely to depend on a collaborative relationship between human marketers and intelligent technologies.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence in Software Engineering: From Code Generation to Reasoning
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has become one of the most influential technologies shaping software engineering in recent years. This transformation has moved beyond early code generation and completion tools toward systems capable of participating in requirements analysis, design, testing, debugging, documentation, and solving complex software problems. The aim of this review paper is to examine the evolving role of AI in software engineering, with a particular focus on the transition from code generation tools to reasoning-based infrastructures. In this study, relevant research and studies on the application of Large Language Models (LLMs), code generation tools, and intelligent systems across different phases of the software development lifecycle are reviewed and categorized. The distinction between automatic code generation and capabilities such as problem analysis, planning, multi-step reasoning, and solution evaluation is also discussed. Findings from the reviewed literature indicate that AI can evolve from an auxiliary tool for generating code fragments into an effective factor in supporting more complex software engineering processes. However, issues such as output correctness, reasoning errors, code security, dependence on training data, trustworthiness, and the necessity of human oversight remain significant challenges in this field. Finally, the paper emphasizes the need to move from a purely "code generation" perspective toward a more comprehensive approach based on human–AI collaboration in software engineering processes.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence in the Intergenerational Transmission of Religious Values: New Challenges for the Family and Upbringing from the Perspective of Catholic Personalist Anthropology
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly becoming part of the environments in which religious questions are explored, and values are interpreted and transmitted across generations. Although existing scholarship addresses digital religion and the ethical and educational implications of AI, the mechanisms through which conversational AI may influence intergenerational religious communication within families require further conceptual examination. This article develops a Responsible Relational AI Mediation Model grounded in family pedagogy, religious socialization theory, digital religion studies, AI ethics, and Catholic personalist anthropology. This study employs an interdisciplinary conceptual approach based on critical literature analysis and synthesis, supplemented by selected international policy documents and Catholic Church teaching. The proposed model integrates three analytical dimensions: structural, identifying the persons, relationships, communities, and technologies involved in religious formation; processual, examining how AI-generated interpretations may influence perceived authority and intergenerational dialogue; and normative, establishing criteria for responsible technological mediation. It distinguishes between relationally integrated and non-integrated pathways of AI-mediated religious inquiry and recognizes generative AI as an educational tool, a mediator of interpretation, and a potential environment for ongoing religious learning. This article argues that the formative significance of AI depends on how its use is connected with critical discernment, interpersonal relationships, and religious community participation. The model offers a conceptual framework for future empirical research rather than establishing causal effects of AI on religious formation.

items.title: Artificial intelligence leadership in nursing management for Nursing Organisations: A Concept Analysis
items.abstract: Background: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly embedded in nursing management through workforce modelling, quality surveillance, resource allocation and organisational decision support. However, artificial intelligence leadership in nursing management remains conceptually underdeveloped, particularly regarding governance, accountability and nursing-specific leadership responsibilities. Objective: To analyse and define artificial intelligence leadership in nursing management and develop a conceptual framework for future empirical research, competency development and responsible AI implementation. Design: A concept analysis using Walker and Avant’s eight-step methodology, supported by a structured search to identify conceptually relevant interdisciplinary literature. Setting: Peer-reviewed interdisciplinary literature and authoritative policy and professional guidance documents identified through PubMed, Google Scholar, Europe PMC, ProQuest Nursing & Allied Health Database and relevant authoritative sources, published between 2020 and 2025. Main outcome measures: Defining attributes, antecedents, consequences, model cases and empirical referents. Results: Twenty-four substantive sources were retained for conceptual analysis; methodological and theoretical foundations were used separately to guide analysis and support theoretical positioning. Artificial intelligence leadership in nursing management was conceptualised as a governance-specialised extension of nursing leadership comprising five interrelated attributes: strategic AI direction-setting, managerial AI literacy, ethical and regulatory oversight, organisational change leadership and workforce capability development, and systematic integration into nursing management processes. Antecedents were organised as core or contextual conditions; consequences were differentiated into proximal and proposed distal consequences, the latter requiring empirical validation. Empirical referents were identified at individual, workforce and organisational levels. Conclusions: Artificial intelligence leadership in nursing management clarifies the leadership responsibilities required when AI informs nursing managerial decision-making, including algorithmic accountability, human oversight and preservation of professional nursing judgement. The concept provides a foundation for competency development, empirical validation and organisational governance across health and aged care settings, including Asia-Pacific contexts.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Technologies in Financial Services and Fintech
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) increasingly supports financial decision-making, risk assessment, service innovation, and customer interaction. This study maps the Web of Science (WoS) -indexed literature on AI technologies in financial services and financial technology (FinTech) through a PRISMA-guided bibliometric analysis of 512 English-language articles published from 2016 to 2025. Performance analysis, VOSviewer co-word mapping, CiteSpace timeline analysis, and keyword burst detection are combined to examine publication patterns, research contributors, thematic structure, and changes in scholarly attention. The selected corpus shows rapid publication growth and three prominent co-word domains: AI-driven FinTech innovation, machine learning for credit risk and fraud detection, and user adoption of digital financial services. Temporal mapping and the recent burst of the keyword 'trust' indicate increasing scholarly interest in governance-related and user-oriented concerns, alongside established technical applications. These trends also highlight the relevance of environmental, social, and governance (ESG) considerations, particularly AI sustainability, financial inclusion, and responsible governance. Drawing on these observed patterns, the study advances a socio-technical interpretation in which trustworthy AI governance is proposed as a conceptual linkage among innovation, risk management, and user adoption. The framework is an interpretive synthesis, not an empirically validated causal model. Because the study uses a predefined WoS-only search without formal cross-database or search-strategy sensitivity testing, the findings apply to the selected corpus and should not be regarded as exhaustive of the global literature. The resulting research agenda emphasises responsible management of information resources in AI-enabled financial services.

items.title: Artificial intelligence tools for developing research and academic writing skills among graduate students: An action research study
items.abstract: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) has transformed higher education by providing tools that support research and academic writing. This action research study examined changes in graduate students' research and academic writing outcomes following a structured six-week instructional intervention integrating Perplexity AI and Jenni AI. Seventeen graduate students participated in workshops on the effective and ethical use of both tools. Data were collected using pre- and post-intervention questionnaires and an analytical rubric evaluating students' research papers. The mean rubric score increased from 62.51 (SD = 9.80) to 86.47 (SD = 6.59) out of 100, t (16) = 8.26, p < .001, 95% CI [17.81, 30.10], Cohen's dz = 2.00. The overall questionnaire mean increased from 3.17 (SD = 0.56) to 4.42 (SD = 0.51) on a five-point Likert scale, t (16) = 7.99, p < .001, 95% CI [0.92, 1.59], Cohen's dz = 1.94. Participation in the structured AI-supported intervention was associated with substantial improvements in research-paper performance and self-reported research, writing, and AI-related outcomes. The findings also underscore the importance of ethical use, critical evaluation, and human oversight. Given the small single-group design, the results should be interpreted as evidence of pre–post change rather than proof of a causal effect attributable to either AI tool.
